findings.title: Accidental git submodule `sentry-repo` committed to the repository root
findings.body: The commit adds a `sentry-repo` gitlink/subproject pointing to commit `a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a` with no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry. This looks like a nested checkout of the repository that was staged by mistake and will break `git submodule` commands for anyone cloning the repo.

findings.title: Shared cache key uses Python's randomized `hash()` and caches stale allowlist state across processes
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` build the shared-cache key with `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))`. In Python 3, `hash()` is salted per process (`PYTHONHASHSEED`) and only affects tuples when they contain hashed elements or across interpreter restarts/hash-seed differences; more importantly, `hash()` can collide across different project-id tuples, causing an organization's query over an un-allowlisted project set to reuse a cached `True` from a different project set. Furthermore, `sentry.options.get(...)` already has an in-memory TTL cache backed by `default_store`, and nothing in the codebase calls `invalidate_upsampling_cache` when the option `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` is updated, so this extra cache layer both risks cross-project collisions and serves stale results in tests and production (for example, in `OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest`, if two tests in the same process used the same `(org.id, project_ids)` pair with different mocked option values, the second test would read the first test's cached result).

findings.title: Upsampling check uses outer `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset` and ignores the rewritten `query`
findings.body: Inside `_get_event_stats`, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` is called with the outer `dataset` and `request` rather than the `scoped_dataset` and `query` passed into `_get_event_stats`. When `get_event_stats_factory` splits a dashboard widget query (lines 362-452), it calls `_get_event_stats` with `scoped_dataset=discover` and a modified `query` (e.g. `f"({query}) AND !event.type:transaction"` or `f"({query}) AND event.type:transaction"`), while the outer `dataset` is `metrics_enhanced_performance` or `metrics_performance`. Because `dataset` is not `errors` or `discover`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` always returns `False` for those split queries; conversely, if `request.GET["query"]` contained `event.type:error` and `_get_event_stats` was called for the transactions-only split query, checking `request` instead of `query` would wrongly treat the transaction query as an error query.

findings.title: Unrelated change to `topEvents <= 0` error message breaks existing endpoint tests/contract
findings.body: Line 124 changes the 400 error detail from `"If topEvents needs to be at least 1"` to `"topEvents needs to be at least 1"`. While the original phrasing had a typo, this change is unrelated to error upsampling and alters the response body expected by existing callers/tests for `OrganizationEventsStatsEndpoint`.

findings.title: `upsampled_count` sums `sample_weight` without handling `0` or NULL/default weights for non-sampled events
findings.body: `upsampled_count` is defined as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` with `private=False` (the default on `SnQLFunction`). For events in allowlisted projects that were ingested before client error sampling was enabled or from SDKs that do not send a sample rate, `sample_weight` in Snuba can be `0` or unset, causing `sum(sample_weight)` to count those events as `0` instead of `1` (e.g. `sum(if(greater(sample_weight, 1), sample_weight, 1))` or `coalesce`). Additionally, omitting `private=True` exposes `upsampled_count()` as a user-queryable function on the discover dataset for any organization, bypassing the project allowlist check.
